children.node_title: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF INFORMATION SECURITY:

attributes.name: Details
attributes.value: The  main  goals  of  determining  the  roles  and  responsibilities  of information security are to clarify the roles of individuals, identify accountability,  maintain  segregation  of  duties,  and  to  omit  any conflict of interests. Therefore, to develop a complete information security strategy, policy and corresponding program in the entity, all roles and responsibilities in relation to information security should be clearly set and defined as tentatively and generically suggested below or in any other entity-specified approach that doesn't conflict with the requirements of this control:

children.node_title: Board of Directors
The board of directors should accept the responsibility of information  security  and  present  commitment  towards it;

The  entities  board  of  directors  is  assigned  the  responsibility  of  overseeing  a  properly  managed  and  implemented information security program/management system and reviewing risk assessment reports.
Director General/CEO
The CEO or Director General who might be reporting to the board of directors has responsibility for:
Accepting and endorsing the overall responsibility of information security;
Enforcing  organization  wide  information  security management system;
Enforcing  information  security  policies  implementation across the entity;
Overseeing and monitoring organization's compliance to  information  security  management  system  and information security policies;
Enforcing accountability towards information security.
Information Security Steering Committee

An information security steering committee, headed by Director  General  or  Deputy  (who  is  not  responsible  for implementing  operational/technical  security  controls), should be established and should include members who are  heads  from  each  division/business  function  in  the entity.  The  steering  committee  should  maintain  the  following roles and responsibilities:
Supervise  and  ensure  the  implementation  of  an information  security  management  system  and  its controls across the entity;
Conduct periodical reviews on the implementation of information security regulation and any information security controls and objectives;
Review  and  approve  periodically  the  information security policies and procedures for implementation within the entity;
Promote information security culture within entity.
Ensure  that  relevant  information  security  methodologies  are  part  of  all  business  processes  and  any new  initiatives or projects across all the entity departments or functions;
Follow  up  and  review  both  internal  and  external audits results for effectiveness of Information Security Regulation implementation and ensure necessary and timely corrective actions are taken;
Review  and  approve  the  information  security  risk assessment methodology and decide on the criteria for acceptable level of information security risks/risk appetite;
Ensure  that  adequate  resources  are  provided  to implement,  support  and  operate  the  information security management system;
Make  recommendations  for  both  corrective and preventive  actions  based  on  the  risk  assessment approach;
Review the Information Security Incidents and their responses;
Ensure that recommendations approved by the committee are implemented;
Ensure  that  Information  Security  requirements  are integrated  as  part  of  contractual  requirements  in their respective project management activities;
Review and approve risk assessment based treatment plans and any residual risks, to be applied across the entity.
Senior Management
The entities senior management is assigned the following responsibilities:
Ensure  that  each  employee  understands  his/her information security-related responsibilities and acknowledges  through  a  formal  sign-off  that  he/
Determine  the  criticality  and  business  risk  of  their information systems and information assets;
Periodically assess information assets and their associated risks;
Communicate the risk assessment results to relevant stakeholders;
Determine and review the access privileges related to their information assets and information systems on a periodic basis;
Implement  information  security  policies  and  procedures to cost-effectively reduce risk to acceptable levels;
Periodically,  ensure  conducting  technical  security testing on the information systems;
Ensure  reporting  of  any  evidence  of  information security  compromise or any suspicious activity that could potentially expose, corrupt or destroy entities information;
Respond to information security incidents;
Ensure  that  information  security  requirements  are incorporated on respective department's project activities/contracts.
Information Security Position

Dubai  Government  Entity  allocates  the  responsibility of information security to a dedicated person or a team. The person heading the information security governance team should be an UAE National, qualified, capable and independent,  reporting  to  the  top  management,  while considering the segregation of duties and omitting any conflict  of  interests.  Hence,  the  information  security position is assigned the following responsibilities:
Plan, implement and maintain an information security program/management  system  that  is  integrated with the whole entities processes;
Coordinate  with  the  senior  management  on  the identification, development, secure handling and management of entity wide information assets;
Plan,  develop  and  maintain  an  organization  wide information  security  risk  assessment  methodology in  coordination  with  the  higher  management  in  the entity;
Ensure  that  appropriate  operational  controls  are selected and implemented according to the results of the risk assessment;
Develop the required policies, and procedures, based on results of the risk assessment, in coordination with respective business owners;

Ensure organization wide compliance to the information security program/management  system  and report ISR implementation  status and performance measurement results to the information security steering committee;
Assist  and  support  senior  management  with  their information security responsibilities;

Plan  appropriate  and  periodic  information  security related  awareness,  training,  and  education  within the  entity  and  other  organizational  stakeholders (including partners,  third-party  vendors,  consultants etc.);
Ensure implementation of DESC  issued policies, standards, and DESC certified providers are engaged for related activities;
Employees

The entity assigns all employees responsible for adhering to the information security policies/processes/program and  for  reporting  any  security  breaches  or  incidents  to their direct management;

Employees  and  third  party  user  understand,  agree  and sign  the  information  security  related  responsibilities, follow rules for the acceptable use of entities information and information assets.
Information Security Champions

Senior  management  assigns  the  coordination  of  information security activities to employees who are knowledgeable and aware of information security

regulatory requirements, acting as Information security champions/representatives/coordinators across divisions with following key responsibilities:
Ensure ISR related controls are implemented within the business function in alignment with entity policies and procedures;
Assist business/information owners, project managers in the areas of information security requirements,  risk  assessment,  information  security KPIs, audit related corrective actions etc.;
Participate  in  information  security  related  incident resolution process related to the business function;
Assist  in  conducting  regular  information  security awareness to their respective business function users.
Internal Audit
Assign  responsibilities  of  auditing  the  implementation effectiveness  of  the  information  security  regulation requirements to an independent audit team/function or an external party;
Ensure  the  audit  team/auditors  are  selected  appropriately to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process;
Protect access to audit tools, audit records to prevent any possible misuse or compromise.
INFORMATION SECURITY POLICY:
Information Security Policy Document

Develops, distributes and maintains an entity-wide information security policy outlining the basic principles of  protecting  all  the  information  assets  of  the  entity, and  make  all  employees  within  the  entity  and  relevant external parties aware of the potential security threats and associated business risks;
Ensure  the  information  security  policy  is  approved  by top management, published and communicated to employees and relevant external parties.
Information  Security  Policy  Alignment with the Entity Strategy

Aligns  the  information  security  policy  with  the  entity overall strategy to facilitate the implementation of the entities goals and objectives, and to support its business model  without  setting  any  obstacles  in  implementing them;

Align entities policies with DESC  issued standards, framework and policies to ensure effectiveness of cyber security  and  cyber  resilience  as  part  of  adaptation  of cyber security in new technologies;

Define  entities  policies  reflecting  the  principle  that  no user or device can be inherently trusted within or outside entity  network  and  by  continuously  verifying  based  on multiple  factors,  including  device  health,  user  context, and the sensitivity of the requested resources. (Ex. Zero Trust principle).
Review of Information Security Policy

Sets  a  clear  responsibility  for  a  regular  review  of  the information security policy to be conducted at least once a  year,  and/or  along  with  any  changes  that  the  entity might undergo;
Reports any update or review of the information security policy  to  the  Information  Security  Steering  Committee and sets the declaration of changes to the entities CEO/ Director General.
TECHNICAL AND OPERATIONAL POLICIES:

Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  a  set  of  technical/ operational information security policies that covers the required security protection measures and controls based on  the  results  of  the  risk  assessment  and  depicts  the overall responsibility of all stakeholders in safeguarding the respective business process related information assets;

Supplements the entities technical/operational policies, as  necessary,  with  a  set  of  procedures  and  guidelines that cover the implementation details of the policies in accordance with the risk assessment results;

Ensure  entities information  security related policies are  reviewed  and  approved  on  a  periodic  basis  (at  least once  a  year)  to  keep  it  current  in  addressing  potential information security and cyber related threats and minimizing risks related to information assets.
INFORMATION SECURITY AWARENESS AND TRAINING:

Designs, develops, and implements an information security awareness program throughout the year (that is categorized based on job roles, divisions or as the entity specifies)  which  is  composed  of  targeted  information security awareness creation activities in line with entities information security related policies;

Provides basic information security training and awareness  to  all  personnel  within  the  entity,  covering information  security  topics  and  related  entities  policy requirements,  as  part  of  initial  training  for  new  users, when required by information systems changes, and in an entity specified periodic intakes;

Provides  periodic  and  adequate  information  security trainings, to be delivered by skilled/competent resources  for  the  employees  taking  part  in  operating the information security program/management system within their respective business areas;

Designs and maintains the information security awareness materials that educates users on information security policies and covers entities business operations' security risk and focus on reducing possible business risks;

Conduct periodic security awareness surveys to measure the  security  training  effectiveness  and  the  awareness level  of  all  entities  personnel  and  applicable  external parties, in  order  to  point  out  common  mistakes  or misunderstandings in information security concepts, and to improve the overall awareness program;
Documents information security training and awareness attendance records for all personnel;
Determine the appropriate mode (classroom/online/ so/f\_t.ligaware  tool  etc.)  of  training  techniques  or  methods based on the specific organizational requirements;
Entity  uses  its  website/public  portals,  programs,  initiatives  to  spread  cyber  security  awareness  among  its general public community, external parties.
CONFIDENTIALITY AGREEMENTS:

Develops, and regularly reviews a non-disclosure or confidentiality agreement  which  is signed by all employees and external parties, that addresses in legally  enforceable  terms,  the  need  for  protecting  the Government information from being leaked internally or externally, and emphasizing the «need to know» concept;
Educates personnel and makes  them  aware  of the confidentiality  of  government  information  and  how information  leakage,  written  or  spoken,  can  impact  the entity.
RELATIONS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF INFORMATION SECURITY:
Maintains appropriate contacts with relevant authorities within the field of information security;
Identifies  key  contacts  of  certain  security  and  judicial authorities to be contacted in the cases of information security incidents, breaches, etc.;
Maintains interactions and/or memberships with information security interest groups, forums and associations, in order to keep up-to-date information in the field of information security.
SECURING EXTERNAL PARTIES' RELATIONS:

Determines  and  assesses  governance  and  information security risks related to its relations with external parties, such  as  customers,  external  party  services  providers, business consultants, temporary employments, etc. This also includes outsourcing and cloud services providers;
Selects and applies the appropriate information security controls and measures to control the identified risks;

Develops  and  implements  the  required  agreements/ contracts,  to  secure  relations  with  the  external  parties, incorporating  information  security  compliance  requirements, covering integrity, availability and confidentiality.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To identify and classify the information assets, and define the proper storage  and  handling  and  secure  disposal  measures  in  order  to protect the entity from legal liabilities, losses, attacks, etc.

children.node_title: INFORMATION ASSETS MANAGEMENT

Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  an  entity  wide  information  asset  management  policy  and  procedure  or framework for the identification, management and protection of information assets in line with applicable laws and regulations;

Identifies,  documents,  and  maintains  a  register  of  all critical information assets for the entire entity, including the  information  and  data  assets  and  the  related  information  processing  facilities  and  components,  such  as so/f\_t.ligaware  assets,  people  assets,  physical  assets,  etc.  and consider other details such as, information classification, physical location, license details, business value, and any other  necessary  information  that  may  be  required  to avoid risks and recover from disasters;
Respective  business  owners  reviews  and  maintains  the information asset register on a regular basis.
INFORMATION ASSETS OWNERSHIP/ CUSTODIANSHIP

Establishes and implements information ownership policy,  where  information  assets  are  identified  with  an owner and a custodian. Business processes, services, applications, information systems, or set of data are examples of  assets  that  ownership  and  custodianship  should  be allocated to;
Assigns the information assets owner the responsibility of ensuring that proper classifications of information are carried out based on the sensitivity of information;

Assigns the information assets owner the responsibility of defining the proper access control to the information and  ensuring  periodic  review  of  access  in  accordance with assigned classification level and the entities access control policy;

Assigns  the  custodians  the  responsibility  of  maintaining  the  day  to  day  operational  tasks  related  to  the information assets, while considering the higher authority of the assets by the owners.
INFORMATION ASSETS CLASSIFICATION

Defines  and  implements  an  information  classification scheme/process  to  be  used  within  the  entity  based  on information assets criticality, value, legal and protection requirements, etc. in line with applicable laws and regulations (ISR Ref. 11.1 and 11.2);
Develops, distributes and maintains information classification policy and related procedures in line with applicable laws and regulations (ISR Ref. 11.1 and 11.2).
INFORMATION ASSETS LABELING AND HANDLING

Defines and implements adequate labeling and handling controls for the information assets (electronic and physical);  according  to  the  requirements  of  each  classification  level,  considering  the  handling  requirements, storage procedures, distribution limitations, etc., for each information asset;
Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  procedure  for  the information assets labeling and handling requirements.
DISPOSAL OF INFORMATION AND ASSETS
Identifies and implements the required safety and security  measures  prior  to  the  disposal  of  information or information assets based on their value, criticality and sensitivity;
Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  clear  procedure  for the  process  of  disposal  of  information  and  information assets, as part of the labeling and handling procedure;
Maintain records of the disposed critical/classified information in line with information classification scheme.
INFORMATION ASSETS RESPONSIBILITY
Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  an  acceptable  use policy governing the acceptable use of information and assets  including  usage  of  personal  devices  in  entities environment.
INFORMATION/DATA PROTECTION

Define  a  process  for  identifying  critical/classified  information or data (not open and not public data) exposure in line with specific compliance requirements for protection and  privacy,  in  line  with  applicable  laws  and  regulations (Eg. Dubai Data Law);

Ensure  entities  critical  /  classified  information  or  data (not  open  and  not  public  data)  does  not  get  processed, stored  and  shared  outside  the  boundaries  of  the  UAE, without protection measures and necessary approvals;
Define a process for data masking, synthetic data techniques in line with entity policies, business requirements, applicable laws and regulation;
Implement  appropriate  synthetic  data,  data  masking techniques,  based  on  a  risk  assessment,  where  entity critical data being shared with other parties for business purposes;

Implement appropriate data privacy protection controls when  implementing  advance  technology  solutions  and automated response systems (Eg. CHATGPT, AI, IVR etc.) in alignment with entities data classification and risk assessment results.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To  identify  and  treat  risks  associated  with  critical  information  and information assets through a detailed study of business processes, in determining threats and vulnerabilities and accordingly apply the appropriate risk treatment plans and controls.

children.node_title: RISK ASSESSMENT METHODOLOGY AND PLANNING
Develops a risk assessment methodology that aligns with the  requirements  of  the  entities  information  security program/management system;
Determines a periodic plan for conducting the risk assessment across the entity;
Identifies the criteria of acceptable risks as part of the risk assessment methodology;

Identifies  the scope of  the  risk  assessments  involving key  stakeholders  (including  third  parties),  around  their business  processes  and  respective  information  assets that will be included in the assessment;
Ensure information and information system related threat data and vulnerabilities collected and analyzed as part of information security risk assessment process;
Entity should identify, collect and analyze threats related entities critical information and related assets as part of threat intelligence process;
Plans  and  implements  a  periodic  awareness  of  the  risk assessment program across the entity.
RISK ASSESSMENT
Conducts  and  maintains a detailed risk  assessment in accordance with the approved risk assessment methodology;
Analyses risks and prioritizes them based on the criticality, in order to set treatment plans and controls;
Determines and identifies  the  acceptable  risks  in  accordance with the risk assessment methodology;
Documents the risk assessment results and get the high risks  approved  by  the  Information  Security  Steering Committee or top management.
RISK TREATMENT AND MITIGATION
Selects the proper risk treatment plans (mitigate, avoid, transfer, etc.) for the identified risks;
Determines  and  selects  the  appropriate  security  operational  controls  (under  operational  domains  within  this document) for mitigating the identified risks;
Information security steering committee authorizes the implementation of the risk mitigations controls for high risks;
Risk  owner  implements  the  mitigation  controls  for  the risks identified;
Reviews  and  monitors  the  implemented  risk  mitigation controls for effectiveness.
RISK ACCEPTANCE

Documents  the  high  or  similar  category  residual  non treated risks with justifications and gets it signed off from the  Information  security  steering  committee/top  management along with the detailed plan for treatment at a later date.

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: The scope of the information security management program must consider  all  business  processes  and  critical  information  processing facilities and components, including:

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented policy  and  procedure  for  the  management  of  information  security  incidents,  including  the  requirement  for reporting  high  severity  incidents  to  DESC  and  other external authorities;

Establishes a competent and certified capability (incident response team) to follow entities process for the handling of information security incidents and response across the entity, with the following key responsibilities:
Has knowledge on the incident and related processes;
Develop incident management plan, procedures;
Respond and Investigate incidents and determine the root cause;
Report  and  communicate  action  plan  to  relevant stakeholders;
Protect collected incident related evidence;
Identify and record lessons learned and any process improvement requirements.

Identify required training, certifications and provide periodic awareness, on-going professional development for entities  incident  response  team  personnel  for effective handling of information security incidents;
Entity  should  define  and  implement  incident  management process addressing:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: Assessing information security incidents and categorize based on severity;
Appoint qualified/DESC certified incident responders in  case  of  involving  external  parties  for  incident handling;
Reporting  of  high  severity  incidents  to  DESC  for further investigation;

Develop and execute test process to verify effectiveness of  incident  response  process  and  capability  and  where applicable,  identify  additional  controls  to  avoid  similar incidents in the future.

Such information processing authorities are  defined  by  Dubai  Government Entities and must be consistent with their mandates and applicable laws and regulations (in line with ISR Ref. 11.1 and 11.2).

Assigns responsibility to all employees or any users dealing with the entities information (IT and non-IT), through any means, for reporting promptly any observed or suspected information security incidents or weaknesses in systems or services, to the responsible entities team;

Implements an escalation process for reporting information security incidents identified as high severity for the entity and identifies and engages external authorities for further investigation if needed for such incidents.

Any  processing  of  Personally  Identifiable  Information  (PII)  and classified information must be lawful, fair, relevant and not excessive in  relation  to  the  purposes  for  which  they  are  processed.
Implement  a  process  to  identify,  collect, retain  and preserve evidences related to information security incidents.
Such purposes should be explicit, legitimate and determined before the time of collection.
Develops a knowledge base from all information security incidents (IT and non-IT) which includes details of previous incidents, their types, cost, and  any  other relevant information;

Develop a centralized repository to gather data related to information security incidents, attack trends, new threats and vulnerabilities from multiple external sources such as vendor reports, government entities, security alerts, etc. for analyzing and formulate  preventive action plan.
PROBLEM MANAGEMENT
Entity should define and implement a problem management process addressing the following:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: Problem detection;
Categorization and prioritization;
Diagnosis and investigation;
Resolution;
Lessons learned and improvements.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To  secure  and  protect  the  logical  and  physical  access  to  entities information throughout its life-cycle along with information processing facilities, and resources.

children.node_title: ACCESS CONTROL MANAGEMENT POLICY/PROCEDURE

Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  an  access  control policy  that  addresses  all  security  requirements  for  the implementation  of  an  effective  access  control  within the entity, including third party access control and grant access  to  resources  that  are  absolutely  necessary  for  a user or a device with 'least privilege' approach (zero trust approach);
Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  an  access  control procedure that provides implementation details for access control, based on role-bases access control;
Maintains a secure repository of all information systems access controls.
LOGICAL ACCESS CONTROL
Users Access Control
Defines and implements a process for users registration, de-registration, and users access privileges modification, disabling or removal, etc.;
Provides  each  user  with  a  unique  identifier  (user  ID)  for their individual business use only;
Implements a unified users ID standard across the entity;
Implements  a  proper  authentication  technique  for  the validation of claimed identities of users regarding access being onsite and remote;

Develops, distributes and maintains appropriate authentication policy (ies) (e.g. a password management policy  that  clearly  addresses  the  password  allocation process, users' responsibilities on passwords use and the recommended password structure, etc.);
Identifies  the  categories  of  users  requiring  regular  and special  privileges  by  ensuring  the  availability  of  the following:
A valid and approved access authorization;
Intended system usage;
Other attributes as required by the entity or associated missions/business functions;
Utilization of access accounts with special privileges must be restricted for their intended purpose.
Maintains records of all entity and third party users' access privileges, and monitors them on a continuous basis;
Limits  the  number  of  special/high  privileged  user  IDs to  those  individuals  who  absolutely  must  have  such privileges for authorized business purposes;
Implements proper security and independent monitoring controls over the usage of special or high privileged IDs;
Implements proper process for guest and temporary user IDs request and employs automated user IDs termination;
Allocates access privileges based on context established through  least-privileged  access  controls,  separation  of duties and strict user authentication-not assumed trust (zero trust approach);
Employs a process for review and re-authorization of user and third party access rights on a periodic basis, as defined by the entity.
Network Access Control

Develops, distributes and maintains a policy for network access  control,  which  covers  details  about  accessible networks  and  networks  services,  authorization  process for granting network access, etc.;
Defines a process for authorizing, activating and terminating any network connections in the entity;
Implements a proper network access control tool/method for  network equipment/devices connectivity detection, identification and authentication;
Manages  and  controls  access  to  configuration  ports  on network equipment/devices;
Implements proper segregation controls on the different types of networks (internal, external, wireless, IP telephony, etc.);
Implements  proper  security  and  operational  controls for any network connections beyond the entities direct control.
Operating System Access Control
Manages  and  controls access to operating  systems through secure log-on process;
Assigns  each  user  with  a  unique  user  ID  and  apply  the proper authentication method for identity verification;
Limits the use of generic user IDs to only exceptional and business  justified  circumstances,  and  implements  the proper accountability technique for such use;
Implements an entity wide authentication mechanism to enforce various authentication controls;
Manages and controls the use of utility programs;
Implements session time-out controls to prevent unauthorized access;
Implements lock-out policy;
Restricts connection times for critical information systems and applications;
Records and continuously reviews logs of administrators system IDs.
Applications Access Control
Provides access to applications based on job responsibilities  and  business  justifications,  in  alignment with the entity access control policy/procedure;
Implements  proper  physical  or  logical  isolation  controls for  highly  critical  information  systems  and  application environments.
Remote Access Security

Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  a  policy  addressing remote working or remote access to the entities resources and  appropriate  security  measures  are  implemented based on results of risk assessment to protect the entity information/data, for remote working users;
Supplement, as necessary the remote working policy with a  procedure  addressing  secure  remote  connectivity  (Eg. VPN),  personal  device  use,  secured  communication  and user responsibilities;
Enforces formal authorization and appropriate authentication prior to remote access connections;

Ensures that adequate security controls are implemented on  the  VPN  client  machines,  such  as  authentication, encryption, anti-virus so/f\_t.ligaware, personal firewalls, session timeout, content filtering etc.;
Provides remote access users with access to the services, which the users are specifically authorized to use;
Monitors and periodically reviews the remote users access connections and activity logs.
Mobile Computing
Develops, distributes and maintains a documented policy governing the appropriate use of mobile computing and communication facilities;
Implements  appropriate  security  controls  to  protect against the risks of mobile computing and communication facilities' usage, such as:
Implement  encryption  mechanisms  to  protect  sensitive information;
Ensure  secure  handling  for  the  portable  computing devices;
Implement  proper  mechanisms  to  disable  portable computing devices or wipe device data when lost or stolen;
Proper  data  backup  procedures  for  the  portable computing devices;
Limit or restrict usage of portable computing devices to authorized users with adequate security controls.

Develops, distributes and maintains a policy and procedure  for  the  handling  and  usage  of  personally  owned devices bring your own device (BYOD) that are not owned by the entity, addressing entities security requirements on  handling  lost  or  stolen  portable  computing  devices, storage of entity data on these devices, connectivity to entity network and systems etc.;
Wireless Access Management
Develops, distributes and maintains a documented policy on the wireless network usage;
Authorizes formally the wireless access to the network prior to any connection;
Implements the proper authentication controls for the wireless access;
Enforces proper security controls for wireless connections to the entities network and establishes usage restrictions and implementation guidance for such use;
Provides wireless connection users with access to services that they have been specifically authorized to use;
Monitors continuously the unauthorized wireless access to the network.
PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
Physical Access Control Policy and Procedure
Develops, distributes and maintains a documented physical  access  policy  that addresses the entities  requirements for implementing physical access controls on offices, rooms and other areas;

Supplements,  as  necessary,  the  physical  access  policy with  a  detailed  procedure  on  how  to  implement  the protection  controls  and  provides  users  with  complete specification on physical security safeguards;
Enforces formal authorization prior to physical access to any facilities with information processing resources.
Physical Security Controls
Enforces appropriate physical access control perimeters for all physical access points to the entity;
Verifies and ensures that only authorized employees are provided access to protected areas;
Controls and monitors physical access to the information processing facilities areas or any other public areas;
Safeguards  and  enforces  adequate  protection  controls on physical access devices;
Keeps inventory of all physical access devices owned by the entity;
Reviews logs of physical access on a regular basis;
Deploys mechanism to monitor the movement of employees and non- employees within the entity.
PUBLIC AND EXTERNAL PARTY ACCESS CONTROL
Enforces formal authorization prior to logical or physical access  required  by  external  party  through  deploying a «need to know» criteria;
Monitors and logs logical or physical access provided to public or external party;

Controls  physical  access  to  any  areas  that  includes information  systems  and  other  areas  such  as  delivery, loading, or any other points where unauthorized personnel  may  enter  by  authenticating  visitors  before authorizing access;
Authorizes,  monitors,  and  controls  entering  and  exiting the  data  center  facilities  or  any  other  public  areas  and maintains such records;

Sets physical access protection and control mechanisms on all external parties or outsourced individuals and hold them liable for any violation or compromising the entities information security policy.
INFORMATION AND DOCUMENTS ACCESS CONTROL
Places  adequate  security  controls  on  handling  critical so/f\_t.liga/hard  documents  and  records  to  protect  from  any loss, mis-use or unauthorized access or modification;
Determines and assigns the needed access rights for the protected documents/information;

Sets  a  clear  policy  on  controlling  documents,  along with  defining  a  clear  retention  period  for  archiving,  and supplementing  it  with  procedures  and  guidelines  for implementation and usage;
Employs a procedure for the disposal of documents, with requirements of authorization and responsibilities.
ACCESS CONTROL AUDIT AND REVIEW
Implements audit trails in information processing systems, as necessary;
Logs, maintains  and  periodically reviews logical  and physical access control lists.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To  set  controls  for  mitigating  the  risks  associated  with  the  daily operations of information processing systems, applications, network and communication tools being used internally and/or with external party.

children.node_title: All  Dubai  Government  Entities  and  their  employees,  consultants, contractors and visitors are required to be aware of the consequences of not following the guidelines set by Information Security Regulation.
Technology  and  Operations  Capacity Management:

Ensures advanced planning and preparation for availability  of  adequate  capacity  and  resources  for  the information  processing  systems  and  their  technology components, and in line with applicable regulations;
Conducts an annual projection review of capacity requirements and resources for the information processing  systems  and  their  technology  components, integrating business requirements.
Documentation of Operational Procedures:
Develops  and  maintains  a  complete  set  of  operating procedures documentations of all information processing systems detailing inputs, outputs and dependencies;
Documents and maintains up to date baseline configurations  manuals  of  all  information  processing systems  including an inventory of essential  system components;
Has documented cyber security standard/guidelines for procurement/development of systems or applications;

Places  adequate  security  protection  controls  on  the documentation  of  operational  procedures  of  all  critical information processing systems, through defining a clear distribution  list  and  permitted  users  and  ensures  their availability to authorized users whenever required.
Change Management:

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented change  management  policy  that  defines  the  overall change  management  process  employed  by  the  entity, outlining roles and responsibilities of different business owners;

Supplements,  as  necessary,  the  change  management policy with a detailed procedure to facilitate the implementation of the change and configuration management process and provide guidelines for all users;
Implements  a  change  management  process  that  must include the following details, as a minimum:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: Description of required change;
Testing and implementation plans for the change;
Risk assessment of the change impact;
Official authorization of the change and the communication process for all stakeholders;
Rollback process for recovery of unsuccessful changes.
Segregation of Duties:

Segregates duties and responsibilities as necessary through  distributing  the  tasks  for  a  specific  business process/area among multiple users, in a manner to reduce errors, fraud and unauthorized modification or misuse of the entities assets.
Separation of Operational Facilities:

Segregates  where  necessary  development,  testing  and production processing facilities to mitigate the risk impacting  the  production  systems  from  unauthorized intentional or unintentional access or change;
Allocates  secured  computing  environment  for  the  sensitive and critical information systems facilities;
Information Systems Deployment:

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented policy  and  procedure  for  the  acquisition,  deployment and  upgrade  of  information  systems,  addressing  the entities requirements for ensuring proper security controls implementation and in line with entities baseline configuration requirements, prior to acceptance or deployment;

Defines  and  implements  proper  acceptance  criteria  for new information systems implementation and upgrades, and enforcing formal certification and accreditation process outlining security requirements;
Carries  out  suitable  security  testing  of  the  information systems during development and prior to acceptance and deployment, and ensures periodic testing.
Virtualization Techniques:

Employs  virtualization techniques, as  necessary  and whenever  applicable,  along  with  deployment  of  the proper  security  controls,  which  can  help,  when  properly implemented,  in  reducing  the  likelihood  of  successful security attacks;
EXTERNAL PARTY SERVICES MANAGEMENT:
Develops, and maintains a formal agreement with the external party service providers that addresses compliance with the entity information security requirements;

Places adequate measures to assure that security controls,  services  definitions  and  delivery  levels  agreed upon  in  the  external  party  contractual  agreements  are implemented and followed by the external party;
Monitors, reviews and audits the services and all related deliverables provided by external party in a regular basis;
Places  adequate  measures  to  manage  and  assess  risks related to changes of the external party services. Examples of changes may include:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: Application of new or enhanced security controls;
Updating entities policies/procedures;
New technology or new vendor to be used.
PROTECTION AGAINST MALICIOUS AND MOBILE CODE:
Develops, distributes and maintains a formal policy covering the requirements for prevention, detection and recovery controls against malicious codes;
Conduct  regular  awareness  across  the  entity  on  the importance of protecting the entity infrastructure from malicious code attacks;
Implements a proper entity wide system/so/f\_t.ligaware for the malicious code scanning, detection and repairing;
Keeps an up to date malicious code protection mechanisms which are continuously updated;
Performs periodic  scans  of  all  information  systems  and real time scans of files from external sources as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed, as defined by the implemented policies;
Automates  the  anti-virus  so/f\_t.ligaware  configurations,  updates and operations among all users and employees;
Establishes and maintains appropriate informative communication channels to obtain latest details of new malicious code;
Develops and implements proper continuity plans/ procedures for recovery from malicious code attacks;
Defines  the  acceptable  and  unacceptable  mobile  code technologies;
Establishes usage restrictions and implementation guides for the acceptable mobile code technologies;
Enforces  formal  authorization,  monitoring  and  control over the use of mobile code technologies.
NETWORK SECURITY

Implements documented process for its network services to  govern  the  interconnections  between  its  network, critical  owned  business  information  systems  and  other networks  and  information  systems  outside  its  formal boundaries,  outlining  the  roles  and  responsibilities  of securing  the  connections  and  all  other  requisite  issues such as duration of connection, ports, users' access, etc.;
Develops  and  implements  network  service  agreements and  ensures  that  all  required  security  controls,  service levels,  and  management  requirements  are  included  in such agreements;
Enables clock synchronization on all networking devices with agreed  reference such as  Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to facilitate forensic analysis, and continuously monitor its accuracy;
Monitors the information system connections continuously and always verifies enforcement of security requirements;
Implements secure network routing controls;

Implements adequate protection level for the
confidentiality,  integrity  and  availability  of  transmitted information and, prevent unauthorized access to information or data in transit (whether within entity or to external network);
Terminates network connections associated with communication  sessions  as  per  the  entity  defined  time period of inactivity;
Implement  measures  to  ensure  adequate/high  level  of network availability;

Configures the network traffic devices on a need basis, as the general rule of thumb is «deny-all» otherwise justify, with  maintaining  logs  of  all  changes  as  per  the  entities change management policy;
Develops and maintains full documentation  of the network devices, connections, and IP configuration while ensuring highest security protection and controls on the documents;
Applies  appropriate  logging  and  monitoring  procedures to enable recording of network security activities;

The entity shall identify and define minimum security and compliance  requirements,  service  levels  of  all  network or  security  services  and  include  these  requirements  in respective  outsourced  or  managed  services  contract  or agreement;

Ensure ongoing monitoring of users and devices on the entity  network  focusing  on  minimizing  risks  related to  threats,  malware  etc.  and  improve  security  posture, prevent data breaches on the network.
INFORMATION EXCHANGE MANAGEMENT:
Information Exchange:

Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  documented  policy and procedures governing the exchange of information internally in the entity, or externally with outside entities, in  all  types  of  communication  channels,  based  on  the criticality of information and in line with relevant laws and regulations;

Develops  and  maintains  formal  information  exchange agreements that cover the protection and non-disclosure requirements  for  the  exchange  of  any  government related information between the entity and any external party;
Applies adequate security controls on top of the process of  exchanging  information,  specifically  for  transmitted physical  media  containing  information  such  as  labeling, liability, etc.;
ELECTRONIC MESSAGING/EMAILS:

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented electronic  communication  policy  that  governs  the  use of  all  electronic  messaging/email  tools  provided  to  the users, outlining the risks associated with it;
Implements mechanisms to ensure confidentiality, integrity and appropriate availability of electronic messaging/emails;
Deploys a process of stamping a mandatory disclaimer for electronic messaging/emails;
Deploys  an  archival  and  retention  policy  for  electronic messaging/emails;
Deploys advanced authentication mechanisms for access to electronic messaging/emails from non-trusted networks and public networks;
Deploys  non-repudiation  supporting  advanced  encryption mechanisms (e.g. digital signatures) while exchanging critical and sensitive government information.
ONLINE TRANSACTIONS AND PUBLIC INFORMATION MANAGEMENT:
Online Transaction Controls:

Implements adequate confidentiality, integrity and availability controls over any online transactional information/services, in order to protect it from frauds, unauthorized modification or disclosure, etc.;

Develops and implements the required agreements with any involved party in  managing the online transactions services,  and  ensures  the  inclusion  of  trading  terms, details of authorization, liabilities, etc.
Public Information:

Protects  the  integrity of public information  that  is available on  publicly  accessible  channels  or  systems such as internet websites, associated written media etc., using information security controls such as appropriate
authentication  and  access  controls,  depending  on  the nature of the business requirements and applicable legal obligations;

Ensures compliance of information published by employees  on  behalf  of  the  government  entity  with applicable  laws,  rules  and  regulations  and  approves  the publication  by  an  authorized  management  body  within Dubai Government Entity.
MEDIA HANDLING MANAGEMENT:
Implements  adequate  security  and  protection  procedures  for  any  type  of  media  containing  information,  in terms of handling, storage, disposal, etc.
MONITORING AND LOGS MANAGEMENT:
Enables audits logs for all information processing systems/applications, and periodically reviews such logs and ensures applying adequate retention measures over them;
Sets adequate monitoring requirements for all information systems/applications based on criticality of the systems;
Logs system administrators and operators activities and ensures reviewing them periodically, by an independent unit;
Enables  faults  logging  on  all  system  levels  including network,  applications,  servers  and  databases  among others;
Deploys  adequate  logs  analysis  mechanism  and  places appropriate actions on faults;
Secures,  where  appropriate,  logging  systems  and  log files against unauthorized changes including alterations, deletions,  and  renaming  of  log  file  contents,  dates  and time stamps;
Sets an appropriate life time for maintaining the logging information, as per the business needs and criticality of information;
Enables clock synchronization over all information processing systems/applications with accurate time source.
DATA CENTER SECURITY:

Define and implement data center security policy based on  a  risk  assessment,  addressing  the  required  logical, physical and environmental protection and security measures  to  secure  entities  data  center  and  related aspects;
Multi-factor authentication should be implemented as  part  of  data  center  access  control,  which  requires the  use  of  two  or  more  different  factors  to  achieve authentication/access;
List  of  authorized  individuals  with  data  center  access (logical and physical) along with approval records, should be maintained identifying the justification for access;

Entry log should be maintained to record person movement in and out of data center with date, time and purpose of visit etc. Physical and logical access lists and logs should be reviewed/audited regularly;
Data  center  assets  related  installations,  changes  must be  formally  approved  and  documented.  These  records should be periodically reviewed by an independent team;
Data centers should be equipped with CCTV for monitoring and the activities therein and will be recorded and  records  retained  as  per  entities  retention  policy requirements;
Procedures  should  be  defined  to  explain  the  process  of handling emergency situations within the data center.
DIGITAL SERVICES:
Identify,  plan  and  implement  entities  digital  services  in accordance with the laws and regulations;
Ensure the approved digital services are made available through  digital  channels  in  line  with  laws,  regulations, Government policies, information security and business continuity requirements;
Periodic  audits  are  conducted  to  ensure  compliance  to security,  privacy  and  data  protection  aspects  of  digital services.
SOCIAL MEDIA
Define  and  implement  a  policy  for  secure  usage  and management  of  social media, considering the risks associated with it and applicable laws and regulations;
Supplements the defined social media policy with detailed procedure addressing the following as a minimum:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: Account creation, management, security and administration;
Information sharing and content management;
Privacy protection;
Monitoring and log management;
Incident management.

attributes.name: Objective

children.node_title: Dubai  Government  Entities  must  conduct  an  applicability  review of  the  Information  Security  Regulation  domains  and  controls  to determine  which  of  these  domains  and  controls  are  applicable  to them.

Define  and  implement  business  impact  analysis  process covering  all  critical  business  process,  critical  services, related  information  systems  and  where  applicable  in alignment  with  Critical  Information  Infrastructure  (CII) guidelines, guidelines for developing the cyber resilience plan issued by DESC;
Periodically conducts a business impact analysis based on the defined process, to define and determine the impact of potential operational failures;
Sets  and  accounts  the  responsibility  of  the business impact analysis to the senior management, with involvement from all related divisions;

Define  and  implement  cyber  resilience/SOC  framework to  establish  high  level  of  cyber  security  focusing  on measuring cyber risk pattern and attack modes for recovering from any cyber attack.

Dubai Government Entities must commit resources to achieve the 'right-fit' implementation, while considering the risk assessment results, and keeping the controls implementation cost lower than the anticipated risk or value of information, which is being protected.
Organizes  and  accounts  responsible  a  committee  of senior management and business owners for the business continuity plan, with defined and clear responsibilities;
Develops, maintains and periodically tests and reassesses a business continuity plan that covers the following:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: The  plan  should  be  based  on  the  business  impact analysis and risk assessment;

The  plan  should  include  at  a  minimum  the  purpose,
scope,  activation  criteria,  implementation  process, internal  and  external  inter-dependencies,  resource requirements,  protect  information  and  information assets during any disruption etc.;
The plan should also address requirements for resilience, alternative processing and recovery capability of all critical business and IT services;
The  plan  should  also  cover  usage  guidelines,  roles and responsibilities, procedures, communication processes, and the testing scenarios and approach.
Designs  a  business  continuity  process  in  a  manner  to reduce the impact of a major disruption on key business functions and processes.

For  deviation  or  an  exemption  to  any  portion  of  the  regulation  is required, a formal written request to DESC is to be submitted with approval from top management of the requesting Dubai Government Entity.
Identifies the most critical business systems and applications in accordance with the risk assessment conducted by the entity;
Deploys a proper recovery plan for the identified critical business systems, as the entities operations specify;
Determines the type of recovery scheme that is applicable for its requirement;
Exercises and periodically tests the decided recovery plan;
Implements disaster recovery sites in case their business systems result in a major loss for the whole government, through using an effective approach based on feasibility studies.
The request must include the description, justification for the exemption along with related risk assessment.
Backup and Storage Policy and Procedure
Develops, distributes and maintains a documented backup, storage and retention policy that includes:
Users' responsibilities;
Requirements for backup and recovery systems;
Backup protection controls;
Legal and business requirements (e.g. recovery point objective, recovery time objective, etc.).
Supplements,  as  necessary,  the  backup  policy  with  a detailed procedure for backup and storage specifications and implements them.
Media Library and Resources Protection
Develops, distributes and maintains a documented policy and  procedure  on  media  library  protection,  including disposal or reuse of media;
Restricts  and  continuously  monitors  access  to  media libraries and storage resources;
Marks clearly all media and storage resources, indicating distribution  lists,  handling  controls,  and  the  application assets security classification as per the assets classification policy;
Allocates  proper  locations,  with  adequate  security  and environmental measures and controls for the storage of the backup media, whether onsite/offsite, as the entity specifies;
Sets security agreements and proper security protection controls in case an external party is involved in handling the media library for the entity;
Protects and controls all physical media while being in a transit process;
Encrypts backups and archives where technically feasible and appropriate;
Maintains accountability for media in transit outside the entity control areas and restricts to authorized personnel.
Backup Testing Restoration
Plans  and  executes  a  periodic  testing  and  restoration process of all backup and storage media.
BUSINESS CONTINUITY PLAN (BCP) TEST AND REVIEW
Maintains,  exercises  and  tests  in  a  periodic  manner  the business continuity plan, disaster recovery plan, backup restoration and related test records maintained;
Plan and execute regular cyber drills activities to test the effectiveness of their resilience plans for critical systems.

attributes.name: Details
attributes.value: The  information  security  regulation  is  broken  down  into  thirteen domains. Each domain takes into consideration one or more major classes  of  information  security:  governance,  operation,  and  assurance.

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: INFORMATION SYSTEMS ACQUISITION, DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT:
Information Systems Acquisition, Development and Management Policy and Procedure

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented policy and procedures for addressing the entities requirements for  ensuring  the  security  on  any  in  house  developed  or external  party  applications  regarding  the  acquisition, development and management of information systems, including mobile applications;

Design  and  implement  'security-by-design'  approach ensuring  that  systems  and  all  their  components  are created incorporating related DESC issued policies, controls  with  proactive  approach  integrating  security from the very start, providing security and privacy.
Application Development

Develops  an  application  or  so/f\_t.ligaware  development  life cycle (SDLC) methodology incorporating adequate security controls at all phases of the so/f\_t.ligaware  development  life  cycle,  while  considering  the  defined  security requirements (e.g. functional, technical, assurance etc.) at each so/f\_t.ligaware development stage;

Defines,  distributes  and  maintains  a  formal  procedure for  secure  deployment,  distribution,  provisioning  and decommissioning of portable computing device applications, application interfaces (APIs) (including third party components), through regular updates/checks to ensure adequate level of security;

Information  and  data  handled  and  processed  by  applications  over  public  networks  is  protected  from  any fraudulent activity, unauthorized modification or disclosure and prevent incomplete transmission.
INFORMATION SYSTEMS SECURITY REQUIREMENTS AND SPECIFICATIONS:

Defines  and  documents  information  security  requirements  in  all  business  cases,  requests  for  proposals  and work  requests, related to acquisitioned or in  house developed information systems, in order to ensure integrating adequate security controls and minimize any cost related to security, and sufficient resources are allocated to implement these controls;

Develops and approves the information systems design documents addressing the security requirements covering all the relevant platforms (e.g. operating systems, browsers, portable computing devices, etc.);
Develops  the  secure  coding  standards  for  information systems  so/f\_t.ligaware/mobile  application/web  application development;
Designs  the  security  architecture  for  the  development and deployment of information systems including network security, transmission security etc.;
Implements  adequate  configuration  management  process  during  information  systems  design,  development, implementation and operation.
SECURE AND CORRECT PROCESSING OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS:
Conducts  proper  testing  to  validate  integrity  of  data input controls on information systems/applications;
Identifies integrity requirements for processed messages and information in the information systems/applications and ensures implementing adequate controls to protect it;
Integrates  validation  checks  into  information  systems/ applications processing to detect any loss of integrity in processed information;
Conducts  proper  testing  to  validate  integrity  of  data output from information systems/applications.
SECURING INFORMATION SYSTEMS FILES, SOURCE CODES AND DATA:
Implements  restrictive  information  system  procedures on  the  installation  and  maintenance  of  so/f\_t.ligaware  in  the operational information systems environments;
Implements  proper  protection  controls  on  the  use  of testing data;
Implements  proper  access  control  procedures  on  information systems/application source codes.
MANAGING CHANGES IN SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT:
Implements proper change management controls on the
so/f\_t.ligaware  development  processes,  whether  performed in-house or outsourced;
Tests and verifies the operational status of all information systems/applications a/f\_t.ligaer implementing any change;
Implements proper controls to limit the risk of changes to so/f\_t.ligaware packages;
Implements proper controls to prevent information leakage in all information system/application environments;
Implements proper security controls on outsourced so/f\_t.ligaware/application  development  covering  all  stages of the project including source  code  management, application maintenance etc.
SECURITY TESTING:

Performs technical security reviews/security audits and vulnerability tests in order to periodically assess technical infrastructure and information systems/applications security against latest threats and vulnerabilities;
Conducts periodic code reviews on all information systems/applications developed in house or by an external party.
DEPLOYMENT OF INFORMATION SYSTEMS/APPLICATIONS:
Deploys the information systems/applications into production  environment  a/f\_t.ligaer  successful  completion  of testing and fixing of identified high risks or critical defects;
Implements security sign off process to confirm the proper implementation  of  security  controls  on  all  information systems/applications prior to deployment.
CRYPTOGRAPHY CONTROLS:
Develops, distributes and maintains a policy on the use of cryptography and key management wherever applicable (e.g. during development and maintenance of information systems/applications etc.);
Implements proper cryptography and key management mechanisms as required by the entity;
Implements proper protection and security controls on all cryptographic keys used by the entity.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To  ensure  protection  of  the  organization  premises,  information processing  facilities  and  resources  from  physical  or  environmental damages.

children.node_title: ENVIRONMENTAL/PHYSICAL THREATS PROTECTION POLICY AND PROCEDURE:
Develops, distributes, and maintains a documented environmental threats protection policy that addresses the entities  requirements  for  placing  environmental protection controls;
Supplements the environmental threats protection policy  with  a  documented  procedure  to  facilitate  the implementation of the environmental threats protection policy.
PROTECTION FROM ENVIRONMENTAL THREATS:
Implements adequate protection controls against environmental threats, such as fire, floods, earthquakes, etc.;
Controls humidity and temperature level on information processing facilities, and continuously monitors it;
Implements proper fire suppression and detection systems;
Implements proper control for monitoring water leakage at the physical information processing facilities.
SECURE WORKING AREAS:
Implements adequate physical  security  mechanisms  on offices, data centres, and other working areas, based on criticality of such areas;
Provides employees with proper guidelines and awareness on  the  implemented  protection  controls  in  the  working areas;

Develops, distributes and maintains a clear desk and clear screen  policy  that  addresses  users'  responsibilities  on securing desks, working areas, and electronic user devices (e.g. PCs, printers, etc.);
Implements  proper  security  controls  over  delivery  and loading areas.
SECURING EQUIPMENT:
Places information systems related equipment in secure and protected locations;
Protects  power  equipment  and  cabling  of  information processing facilities from damages;
Implements UPS (uninterruptible power supply) systems to avoid power failures where deemed necessary;
Implements proper maintenance procedures on all information processing facilities.;
Implements proper protection  controls  over  equipment and  information  processing  facilities  residing  offsite, including its movement, storage and handling;
Implements  adequate  security  controls  on  the  disposal or  re-use  of  any  device  or  equipment  or  information processing facility.
PERIODIC TESTING:
Conducts proper testing and assessment periodically over all  implemented  environmental  and  physical  protection controls, including in data center and records maintained.

hierarchy.node_title: ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF HUMAN RESOURCES

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To ensure that all employees, contractors and outsourced employees are aware of their obligations towards information security and that their  roles  and  responsibilities  are  defined  in  relation  to  securing entities information and its processing facilities.

children.node_title: PRIOR TO EMPLOYMENT SECURITY CONTROLS:
Defines security roles and responsibilities of employees, contractors and outsourced employees in alignment with the entity high level information security policy;
Documents security roles and responsibilities in the job descriptions and objectives of all employees, contractors and outsourced employees;
Conducts proper screening  and  background  verification for  all  employment  candidates,  applicable  third  party personnel according to the applicable laws and policies of Dubai Government;
Ensures  that  all  employment  contracts  define  security obligations  of  employees,  contractors  and  outsourced employees, and that approved candidates read and agree such obligations;
Incorporates  information  security  awareness  as  part  of induction  programs of newly hired employees, contractors and outsourced employees.
DURING EMPLOYMENT SECURITY CONTROLS:
Accounts the senior management responsible for enforcing  compliance  of  their  employees,  contractors and  outsourced  employees  to  the  entity  information security policies and procedures;

Define, implement and maintain documented disciplinary process for employees, contractors and outsourced employees who may breach information security policies and  procedures,  and  maintain  records  of  any  security breaches;
Ensures that all employees, contractors and outsourced employees are provided with information security awareness programs on a regular basis.
TERMINATION/CHANGE OF EMPLOYMENT SECURITY CONTROLS:
Implements  proper  security  controls  on  the  process  of terminating or changing employment;
Communicates termination responsibilities to the terminated employee in relation to confidentiality agreements and employment contracts;
Implements  a  process  for  returning  all  entities  assets upon termination of employment;
Implements  a  process  for  revoking  or  changing  access rights  and  privileges  upon  termination  or  change  of employment.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To  clearly  define  compliance  and  audit  requirements  in  order  to ensure effectiveness of the implemented security controls and avoid any violations and breaches to any laws, policies, or controls.

children.node_title: COMPLIANCE WITH FEDERAL AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT LEGAL REQUIREMENTS:
Ensure compliance with the following laws and regulations and related amendments:
Federal Decree-Law No.46 of Year 2021 on Electronic Transactions and Trust Services;
Law No.21 of 2022, concerning Electronic Transactions and e-commerce;
The Executive Council of Dubai Government Resolution Number  (13) issued in Year 2012  for Information Security Regulation;
The Government of Dubai Human Resources Management Law No. (8) of 2018;
Dubai Electronic Security Center Law No.11 of 2014;
Law  No.26  of  2015  Regulating  Data  Dissemination and Exchange in the Emirate of Dubai;
Law No. (9) of 2022 Regulating the Provision of Digital Services in the Emirate of Dubai;
Federal  Decree-Law  No.34  of  2021  on  Combating Cybercrimes;
Any  other  related  resolutions,  laws  pertaining  to information  security  or  related  to  entities  scope  of services and align with Government's Strategies and related plans.
COMPLIANCE CONTROLS:
Identifies  the  laws  or  regulations  that  are  applicable  to the entities scope of services;

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) policy that defines the legal obligations  pertaining  to  the  use  of  information  assets (e.g. hardware, so/f\_t.ligaware, etc.);
Ensures compliance with Intellectual Property Rights (e.g. so/f\_t.ligaware license agreements);
Prohibits  employees  from  manipulating,  making  or  distributing  unauthorized  copies  of  copyrighted/licensed materials, so/f\_t.ligaware or applications;
Implements  proper  protection  controls  for  the  storage, retention and disposal of entities information assets and records.
PROTECTION OF PRIVATE INFORMATION OF INDIVIDUALS AND CORPORATES:
Develops, distributes and maintains a privacy policy that addresses  the legal  requirements  for  the  prevention  of misuse of personal information of the entities customers;
Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  a  formal  procedure detailing the protection measures required for the processing and handling of private data and information;
Conducts continuous awareness sessions on the requirements of protecting private data and information for the responsible personnel;

Restricts, minimizes and monitors access to personal and private data, and applies proper controls on the process of collecting, processing and transmission of personal data, which should be on «a need-to-know» basis;
Define and implement data leakage prevention measures including  accountability  procedures  to  protect  critical information, systems, devices etc.;

Protect when sharing secret and sensitive data, including personal  data  using  appropriate  protection  techniques (Eg.  data  masking,  pseudonymization  etc.)  in  alignment with entities information classification scheme.
COMPLIANCE WITH INFORMATION SECURITY POLICIES AND STANDARDS:
Conducts periodic reviews to verify compliance of the implemented information security policies and procedures;

Conducts periodic security audits/technical reviews (Eg. VAPT) on information systems to ensure security of entity  critical  systems  and  verify  compliance  with  the policies and security controls/standard;
Periodic  management  reporting  is  done  to  present  the entities  cyber  resilience  status  and  technical  review finding's corrective action details.
AUDIT OF INFORMATION SECURITY REGULATION IMPLEMENTATION:
Plan  and  conduct  periodic  audits  (at  least  once  a  year) across the entity, to ensure the entity is meeting all applicable requirements of information security regulation
including other applicable DESC issued policy, framework and standards requirements;
Report audit findings/recommendations to the top management/information  security  steering  committee  to review appropriate corrective actions;
Periodically follow-up with relevant functions to ensure timely and necessary corrective actions are taken against the audit findings.

attributes.name: Objective
attributes.value: To set controls for mitigating risks associated with cloud computing and usage of cloud services.

children.node_title: CLOUD SECURITY POLICY/ PROCEDURE:

Develops, distributes and maintains a documented cloud security policy that addresses the entities requirements for overall cloud management process including selection, management and exit from cloud  services  and  outlines roles and responsibilities of relevant stakeholders;
Develops,  distributes  and  maintains  a  cloud  security procedure that provides implementation details for establishing and managing secured cloud service environment;
Conducts  periodic  reviews  of  cloud  security  policy  and procedure or if significant changes occur to ensure their continuing suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness;

Perform cloud security risk management that addresses the  entities  requirements  on  using  cloud  computing model (SaaS, PaaS, IaaS etc.) covering Identity and access management, cyber security, data protection, regulatory aspects etc.
CLOUD SECURITY PRINCIPLES:
Data Location

Prevents handling and storing classified data with a cloud service  provider  (CSP),  outside  the  legal  jurisdiction  or geographical  boundaries  of  the  United  Arab  Emirates, including for CSP's backup or disaster recovery purposes.
Data Classification and Handling
Defines and communicates required security controls to cloud service provider (CSP) for handling of data in accordance to the applicable laws and regulations (in line with ISR Ref. 11.1 and 11.2).
Architecture and Deployment Model
Ensures adequate cloud security controls are implemented by cloud service provider (CSP) as per architecture and deployment model approved by the entity.
Service Agreements
Ensures  through  a  formal  agreement  that  the  cloud service  provider  (CSP)  has  no  ownership  rights  on  the stored data regardless of the format or storage medium.

Develops and maintains a formal agreement with DESC approved/certified  cloud  service  provider's  (CSP's)  authorized  services  addressing  the  following  information security requirements as a minimum:

attributes.name: Details

children.node_title: Information security risks and mitigation;
Data protection and storage;
Information security incidents handling;
Change, recovery and restoration;
Data residency;
Data encryption.
Data Portability and Continuity
Ensures that cloud service provider (CSP) has the adequate measures and processes to support data

attributes.name: Details
attributes.value: - migration, data portability whenever the entity decides to moving its data and avoid vendor lock-in issue;

children.node_title: Ensures proper cloud security controls are implemented by cloud service provider  (CSP),  addressing  entities requirements for periodic testing of the continuity and disaster recovery plans and communicating the results to entity.
Compliance and Monitoring:
Conducts periodic reviews or audits to verify cloud service provider's (CSP's) compliance with the applicable security policies and contractual requirements.
